steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for a paper that releases Spanish sequence-to-sequence pre-trained language models (Spanish versions of BART and T5, plus BERT2BERT-style baselines) and evaluates them on Spanish generation tasks. Cover the motivation, background on encoder-decoder models, what we introduce, and a summary of results.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- Spanish NLP resources: encoder-only and decoder-only models, little for generation
- Background: encoder-decoder models (BART, T5), mostly English
- Our models: BARTO, T5S, BERT2BERT-style baselines; Spanish seq2seq benchmark
- Summary of results and release

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Spanish is one of the most widely used languages in the world. Because of this the NLP community has been interested in it and there have been efforts to develop resources for this NLP domain. So a number of pre-trained language models for Spanish have appeared in recent years, mostly using encoder-only and decoder-only architectures. These models have shown very good performance in natural language understanding on several downstream tasks. But there has been limited progress on tasks that are about generating new sentences based on a given input, like summarization, generative question answering, dialogue, or translation.

Encoder-decoder models are mainly used for sequence-to-sequence tasks, and many architectures have appeared in recent years. Pre-training these models is often based on the whole transformer architecture and involves more complicated learning objectives than encoder-only or decoder-only models. For example, BART is trained to reconstruct text that was corrupted on purpose, and T5 is trained to fill in missing parts of text, simulating a scenario where spans of text were left out. These models were developed mostly for English, and there have been recent efforts to pre-train them in other languages. But for Spanish there are very few of these models, even though they could be valuable to the community.

- Our models
  - BARTO, T5S: Spanish counterparts of BART and T5, pre-trained only on Spanish corpora
  - BERT2BERT-style baselines from Spanish BERT and RoBERTa
  - Spanish seq2seq tasks: summarization, QA, split-and-rephrase, dialogue, machine translation
- Results
  - all models good; BARTO, T5S best on generation, esp. long sequences; beat BERT2BERT-style and multilingual
  - discriminative tasks: slightly behind encoder-only in some, still competitive
  - models released

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Spanish is one of the most widely used languages in the world. Because of this the NLP community has been interested in it and there have been efforts to develop resources for this NLP domain. So a number of pre-trained language models for Spanish have appeared in recent years, mostly using encoder-only and decoder-only architectures. These models have shown very good performance in natural language understanding on several downstream tasks. But there has been limited progress on tasks that are about generating new sentences based on a given input, like summarization, generative question answering, dialogue, or translation.

Encoder-decoder models are mainly used for sequence-to-sequence tasks, and many architectures have appeared in recent years. Pre-training these models is often based on the whole transformer architecture and involves more complicated learning objectives than encoder-only or decoder-only models. For example, BART is trained to reconstruct text that was corrupted on purpose, and T5 is trained to fill in missing parts of text, simulating a scenario where spans of text were left out. These models were developed mostly for English, and there have been recent efforts to pre-train them in other languages. But for Spanish there are very few of these models, even though they could be valuable to the community.

In this paper we want to democratize sequence-to-sequence models for the Spanish NLP community, so we introduce BARTO and T5S, which are the Spanish counterparts of the BART and T5 models. These models are pre-trained only on Spanish corpora, following their self-supervised methodology. We also introduce models in the style of BERT2BERT, using well-established Spanish BERT and RoBERTa models as baselines. We also curate a variety of Spanish sequence-to-sequence tasks, like summarization, question answering, split-and-rephrase, dialogue, and machine translation, so that we can assess our models comprehensively.

Our results show that all the models perform well on the proposed benchmark tasks. BARTO and T5S in particular stand out in text generation tasks, especially with long sequences, and they are better than the BERT2BERT-style models and their multilingual counterparts in many generative tasks. We also evaluate the models on discriminative tasks, like sequence and token classification. Their performance is slightly behind encoder-only models in some tasks, but the results are still very competitive. We have made these models available to help future research and practical applications in Spanish NLP.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Spanish ranks among the most widely used languages globally. This has captured the interest of the NLP community, prompting efforts to develop resources for this domain. As a result, a number of pre-trained language models for Spanish have emerged in recent years, predominantly employing encoder-only [1,2,3] and decoder-only [4] architectures. These models have shown exemplary performance in natural language understanding across several downstream tasks [1,5]. Nevertheless, there has been limited progress on tasks that involve generating new sentences from a given input, such as summarization, generative question answering, dialogue, or translation.

Encoder-decoder models primarily serve sequence-to-sequence tasks, and numerous architectures have emerged in recent years. Their pre-training is often based on the whole transformer architecture [6] and entails more intricate learning objectives than those of encoder-only or decoder-only models. For instance, BART [7] is trained to reconstruct text that has been intentionally corrupted, while T5 [8] is designed to fill in missing sections of text, simulating a scenario where text spans have been omitted. These models have been developed predominantly for English, and recent efforts have pre-trained them in other languages [9]. Unfortunately, for Spanish there is a notable scarcity of such models, which may be valuable to the community.

In this paper, aiming to democratize sequence-to-sequence models for the Spanish NLP community, we introduce BARTO and T5S, the Spanish counterparts of the BART and T5 models. These models are pre-trained exclusively on Spanish corpora, following their self-supervised methodology. We also introduce BERT2BERT-style models [10] built on well-established Spanish BERT [11] and RoBERTa [12] models as baselines. Additionally, we curate a variety of Spanish sequence-to-sequence tasks, such as summarization, question answering, split-and-rephrase, dialogue, and machine translation, to assess our models comprehensively.

Our results show that all models perform well on the proposed benchmark tasks. In particular, BARTO and T5S stand out in text generation tasks, especially with lengthy sequences, surpassing BERT2BERT-style models and their multilingual counterparts in many generative tasks. We also evaluate the models on discriminative tasks, such as sequence and token classification; while they are slightly behind encoder-only models in some tasks, they still offer very competitive results. To facilitate future research and practical applications in Spanish NLP, we have made these models available.
